newsitem.title: UK: Three walk free in British soccer-rigging trial.
newsitem.headline: Three walk free in British soccer-rigging trial.

text.p: Footballers John Fashanu and Hans Segers were cleared on Thursday of plotting to rig the results of matches in England's Premier Soccer league.

But, while Zimbabwe-born goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar was also cleared of one match-rigging charge, the jury in one of the most sensational cases in British sport said it still hadn't decided whether he was guilty of a second charge.

Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim, accused with the three of alleged involvement in an Asian gambling syndicate, was also cleared, leaving Grobbelaar as the only remaining defendant in the nine-week-old trial.
Grobbelaar, 39, who has played for his national side as well as Liverpool and Southampton, is charged with corruptly accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,200) to influence the outcome of matches.
He has denied the charge. The jury was sent home for the night and will begin their sixth day of deliberations on Friday.
The trial in Winchester, southern England, is the second the four men have faced. Another jury failed to reach verdicts earlier this year.
Fashanu and Segers emerged from the court, smiling broadly and hugging their wives.

"Its been a nightmare for two and a half years, but we got the verdict we deserved," said Segers, the 35-year-old former Wimbledon goalkeeper. "Today is just an unbelievable day and it has been very emotional."
The Dutch-born player said he was ready to resume his career.
Fashanu, 33, who declined to testify during the court proceedings, said he was not bitter at having had to face two trials.
"Now all I want to do is get on with my family life, my beautiful wife and go back to my friends," he said.
The former Aston Villa and Wimbledon striker is now a popular television presenter and a highly succesful businessman.

The English Football Association announced after Thursday's verdicts that a full inquiry into the case would be carried out the former Deputy Commissioner of London's Metropolitan Police. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
